title: Unlocking the Sports Hub's Full Potential for Singapore
what_it_is: Unlocking the Sports Hub's Full Potential for Singapore

sections.label: Sports Hub PPP agreement
sections.summary: The Sports Hub, anchored by the National Stadium and Singapore Indoor Stadium, has operated since 2014 under a PPP agreement signed in 2010.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It is anchored by the National Stadium and the Singapore Indoor Stadium, with a range of indoor and outdoor sports and retail facilities in the surroundings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It has been in operation since 2014 and was designed, built, financed and operated by Sports Hub Pte Ltd (SHPL) under a Public-Private-Partnership, or PPP, agreement that was signed between SHPL and SportSG in 2010.

sections.label: Government takeover assessment
sections.summary: The assessment is that Singapore's interests would be better served by the Government taking over ownership and management of the Sports Hub.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In our assessment, the interests of Singapore and Singaporeans would be better served by the Government taking over the ownership and management of the Sports Hub instead of carrying on with the PPP arrangement.

sections.label: Sports Hub PPP termination
sections.summary: SportSG served notice to terminate the PPP on 10 June 2022 and will assume full ownership and management on 9 December 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: SportSG formally served notice to terminate the Sports Hub PPP with SHPL on 10 June 2022 and reached a mutual agreement with SHPL over the termination and the process of the handover.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: On 9 December 2022, a few months from now, SportSG will assume full ownership and management of the Sports Hub and begin a new chapter for the Sports Hub.

sections.label: Sporting Singapore Report 2001
sections.summary: The 2001 Sporting Singapore Report stated the former National Stadium had become inadequate to support staging major international sporting events.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2001, the Sporting Singapore Report set out how the former National Stadium, whilst one of the best in Southeast Asia when it was first built, had become quite inadequate to support our ambitions to stage major sporting events of international or world repute.

sections.label: Consortium financing and availability fee
sections.summary: The consortium bore over S$1.3 billion upfront, and the Government paid an annual availability fee of $193.7 million from 2014 until 2035.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The entire sum, an amount in excess of S$1.3 billion, was borne by the consortium upfront and they took out a loan to finance this cost.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Government only started paying the annual availability fee, at $193.7 million per year, subject to inflation and other benchmarking adjustments, when the project was ready and operational in 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Under the terms of the agreement, this was to be paid to SHPL every year until 2035, which is the end of the project agreement period.

sections.label: Construction delays costs
sections.summary: The project encountered construction delays, for which SHPL underwrote the costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For instance, the project encountered construction delays, for which SHPL underwrote the costs.

sections.label: Government cost control measures
sections.summary: The Government ensured costs would not run away by making the consortium bear costs above expectations and return assets at zero cost in 2035.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It was therefore important for the Government to ensure that the costs would not run away.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This was achieved by ensuring that the consortium would have to bear any costs above their expectations and also return the assets back to the Government at zero cost at the end of the project period in 2035.

sections.label: Government right to terminate PPP
sections.summary: The PPP structure gives the Government, but not SHPL, a unilateral right to terminate early, take over ownership and management with no penalty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: But we also envisaged that there could come a time when Singapore would be ready to operate this project, after it has been built – both in terms of expertise in the Government and also growth and maturity of the industry and the broader ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: And that is why the structure of the PPP provides for a unilateral right on the part of the Government, but not SHPL, to terminate the project, to take over ownership and management at any time it wanted, before the expiry of the project, with no penalty for such an early termination.

sections.label: Sports Hub community vibrancy shortfall
sections.summary: The Sports Hub still falls short of promoting sufficient community vibrancy, about eight years after opening in 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, it still falls short of promoting sufficient community vibrancy in and around the Sports Hub.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: At present, it has been about eight years since the Sports Hub first opened in 2014, though the operations of the last two and a half years have affected by the pandemic.

sections.label: Shortfall in Sports Hub events
sections.summary: The quality and volume of events fell short, and apart from Super Rugby 2016-2019, SHPL secured no recurring marquee sport events.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The quality and volume of its calendar of events and programming fell short of what we had envisaged, even taking into account the private sector interest in this project.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Apart from the Super Rugby event from 2016-2019, SHPL has not secured any recurring or marquee sport events at the Sports Hub on a multi-year basis.

sections.label: Social value versus profit-driven model
sections.summary: The profit-driven SHPL model was not sufficiently aligned with the current phase's need for community programming and social outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: But there is an intrinsic social value in realising a young athletes' aspiration to play in the national stadium, cheered on by his or her schoolmates, or having seniors take part in a social event at our iconic stadium grounds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This is where the profit-driven model of the SHPL consortium, which had worked well in the infrastructure phase of the project, was not sufficiently aligned in the current phase of the project, where greater emphasis was needed on community programming and driving social outcomes, even if such programmes did not always resonate with commercial returns.

sections.label: Termination for policy flexibility
sections.summary: Terminating the present arrangement and taking over the infrastructure on a clean break basis would allow better flexibility and discretion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Accordingly, terminating the present arrangement and taking over the infrastructure on a clean break basis, would allow us better flexibility and discretion, in being able to drive our own policy outcomes.

sections.label: Kallang Alive Precinct size
sections.summary: Kallang Alive will be an 89-hectare site along Kallang River and Kallang Basin, about 2.5 times the 35-hectare Sports Hub, transforming by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Kallang Alive will be an 89-hectare site along Kallang River and the Kallang Basin.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For comparison, the Sports Hub is 35 hectares.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, this area of 89 hectares, including the 35 hectares, will be two odd times larger than the current Sports Hub.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This area is envisaged to transform into a vibrant sport, entertainment and lifestyle precinct by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Kallang Alive Precinct development is on a much larger scale and magnitude, as I have said, about 2.5 times that of the 35-hectare Sports Hub.

sections.label: Kallang Football and Tennis Centres
sections.summary: Photos show the Kallang Football Hub, the national training centre, ready by end of this year, and work started on the Kallang Tennis Centre, ready next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I will show Members some photos of the ongoing developments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This includes the Kallang Football Hub, which will be our national training centre, to be ready as soon as the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Here, we see the ongoing construction and a close-up shot of one of the turfs that is already completed and an artist’s illustration of what it will look like when fully completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We have also started work on the Kallang Tennis Centre, which would be ready by next year.

sections.label: Kallang Theatre Precinct tender
sections.summary: SportSG plans to launch a tender to redevelop the Kallang Theatre Precinct into a mixed-use development with an indoor arena, offices, hotel and hospitality offerings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Beyond these sporting assets, SportSG also plans to launch a tender for the redevelopment of the Kallang Theatre Precinct into a mixed-use development, comprising a multi-purpose indoor arena, office spaces to bring sport-related businesses and entities together, commercial facilities, such as a hotel and other hospitality offerings.

sections.label: Combining venues for marquee events
sections.summary: Facilities at OCBC Arena, Singapore Indoor Stadium and the new Kallang Tennis Centre can be combined to bring in marquee sports events such as an ATP1000 tennis event.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For instance, we can seamlessly combine the facilities at the OCBC Arena, the Singapore Indoor Stadium and the new Kallang Tennis Centre and can confidently bring in marquee sports events, such as an ATP1000 tennis event.

sections.label: Government takeover of Sports Hub
sections.summary: After due diligence and a confluence of ecosystem factors, the Government decided to exercise its right to step in, take over ownership and continue managing the Sports Hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I would add that this was not a decision taken lightly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We felt that, however, having done our due diligence, as I have explained at the start and a confluence of these factors in the ecosystem all coming together, this was now a right time for the Government to exercise its right to step in, take over ownership and continue the management of the Sports Hub.

sections.label: Refining PPP framework
sections.summary: The framework is continuously refined using local and international lessons, and PPPs will continue to be leveraged as a model where suitable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This framework is continuously refined and builds on the lessons learnt both here, locally, our own experience, as well as internationally elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will, therefore, continue to be open to leveraging PPPs as a model, where suitable.

sections.label: Government fee to SHPL
sections.summary: The Government would pay SHPL $193.7 million yearly from 2014 until the project's end in 2035.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Second, the Government would pay SHPL a fee of $193.7 million each year from the time the project started operations in 2014 all the way until the end of the project in 2035.

sections.label: PPP committed sum to SHPL
sections.summary: Under the PPP, the Government would pay SHPL about $193 million yearly until 2035, about $2.32 billion from 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, that is the framework of the PPP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Therefore, if we had continued with the PPP arrangement, the Government would continue to pay SHPL approximately $193 million each year, every year, from now until 2035, and that works out, from 2022 onwards, to be approximately $2.32 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That is a committed sum under the PPP.

sections.label: Capital expenditure component
sections.summary: The largest component, about $1.2 billion or over 80% of the total sum, is capital expenditure the Government would bear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Conceptually, the single largest component which accounts for about $1.2 billion, or slightly more than 80% of the total sum to be paid, is the capital expenditure that the Government would have had to bear.

sections.label: Projected termination sum to SHPL
sections.summary: The sum to be paid to SHPL for termination is projected to be around $1.5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: At present, the sum to be paid to SHPL for termination is projected, therefore, to be around $1.5 billion.

sections.label: Full projected termination costs
sections.summary: Adding about $800 million operational costs until 2035 to the termination sum makes full projected termination costs around $2.3 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If we were to draw a parallel comparison against the balance tenure of the Project Agreement, in other words, if you compare like-for-like until the end of the period in 2035, at $68 million per year for operational costs, that brings us to approximately $800 million over the balance period until 2035.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If this $800 million is added to the termination sum, this makes the full projected costs of termination at around $2.3 billion.

sections.label: Costs and termination decision
sections.summary: The costs are capital expenditure and operating expenses, and the decision to terminate was not driven by financial considerations or saving money.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These are simply the costs that we would have had to incur, or would have incurred, going forward, in terms of the capital expenditure and the operating expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I want to make it clear that the decision to terminate the Sports Hub project was not driven by financial considerations or to save money.

sections.label: Taking back Sports Hub ownership
sections.summary: Taking back the Sports Hub from the private sector allows sporting and social objectives to be redefined away from mainly commercial ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We must still operate within financial prudence and ensure that we are not profligate in spending, that we are careful in how we spend.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But, taking back the Sports Hub from the private sector will also mean being able to redefine our outcomes away from being mainly or predominantly commercial in nature, we will be able to better realise our sporting and social objectives, open up the Sports Hub to more Singaporeans and bring greater value and outcomes for us, the future of sports in Singapore, our athletes and the everyday Singaporean.

sections.label: SportSG holding company structure
sections.summary: SportSG will incorporate a holding company to own and operate Kallang Alive assets, with a subsidiary owning and managing the Sports Hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To achieve this, SportSG will incorporate a holding company to own and operate the various pieces of assets within Kallang Alive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: A subsidiary of this holding company will be set up specifically to own and manage the Sports Hub.

sections.label: SHPL employees offered crossover
sections.summary: All SHPL employees have been offered the chance to cross over into the new corporate entity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: All SHPL employees have been offered an opportunity to cross over into the new corporate entity and continue on this mission to make Sports Hub the centre of sports in Singapore.

sections.label: SportSG takeover enables coherent vision
sections.summary: With SportSG taking over, the Government would be better placed to drive a synergised vision for the precinct and provide integrated offerings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Overall, with SportSG taking over, the Government would be better placed to drive a synergised and coherent vision for the whole precinct and achieve internal synergies while providing more integrated offerings and programmes to the public.

sections.label: Handover and future partnerships
sections.summary: SportSG assumes full ownership and management from December this year, with a smooth handover and continued partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The partnership between SHPL and SportSG has given us a strong foundation from which we can now proceed to drive our social and sporting ambitions confidently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And we look forward to working with SHPL for the next few months to ensure a smooth handover and to welcoming SHPL employees to continue with the new corporate entity which we will set up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Even so, as we leave this partnership, as SportSG assumes full ownership and management from December this year, the efforts towards Sports for Singapore still remain a partnership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Between the Government and the private sector partners, we will have to continue to work to provide top-class services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We want to partner with the many community stakeholders, as I have mentioned – students, young athletes, junior athletes, seniors, NSAs and, of course, the many Singaporeans who will participate and make the place even more vibrant and alive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I am, certainly, excited about the potential we will be unlocking, as we build on what we have achieved to turn Kallang Alive into a larger, more diverse and more vibrant sporting and lifestyle hub for everyone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And we cheer our athletes on, as they take on their competitors from around the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, let us write this next chapter together to make Sports Hub and our National Stadium, our Home Ground and a place which we can all be proud of.

sections.label: NDP hosting at Sports Hub
sections.summary: Taking back ownership gives flexibility so cost does not constrain organising events like the NDP at Sports Hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I take it that he was leading the contingent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I think what this taking back of the ownership and management of Sports Hub was designed to do is to give us more flexibility and the ability to not let cost, which was otherwise a serious prohibitive factor, constrain the organisation of events, such as the NDP, at Sports Hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: At the same time, we also want to be circumspect about having it there every year, or even every other year, because there is a five- to seven-month lead time before and after, where much of the facilities will have to be decked up for rehearsals and cannot be used.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, you have to think about it in terms of the programming that we want to do for the Sports Hub, the availability and the options around how to organise the NDP at the Sports Hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But, certainly, Mr Darryl David can be assured that this will be a consideration and, at the very least, the Sports Hub will be open for MINDEF to consider hosting the NDP there.

sections.label: Sports Hub CEO selection process
sections.summary: The passage asks for an update on the selection process and qualities sought for a Sports Hub CEO, and states options are being considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can the Minister give some update about what is the selection process that we can expect, maybe in the months ahead and what are some of the principles or qualities that we would be looking for in a CEO to lead the Sports Hub in its next chapter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We are considering various options for the CEO of the Sports Hub.

sections.label: Sports Hub takeover cost and revenue
sections.summary: The passage states the takeover cost is about $2.3 billion, similar to payments to 2035, and asks if Government shares event revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Minister has explained that the cost of taking over the Sports Hub is about $2.3 billion, which is about the same price as what the Government would have to pay to 2035.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Does the Government take a share in any of this revenue taken from sports or entertainment events?

sections.label: Project agreement cost waterfall formula
sections.summary: The project agreement provides a waterfall formula apportioning costs and payments, with event takings cascading into a fund sometimes shared with Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The project agreement provides for a waterfall formula by which such costs would be apportioned, how payments would be apportioned and the priorities by which they meet the costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There is a formula which cascades down the takings from these events and they are then put it into a fund and, in some cases, shared with the Government.

sections.label: Decision against procurement model
sections.summary: The passage asks why the decision was made when running on the procurement model was quite possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Yes, my first question is, why was the decision made in the first place when it is quite possible that we can run on the procurement model?

sections.label: Fairness of $1.5 billion payment
sections.summary: The passage asks whether it is fair to pay $1.5 billion to SHPL.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: My second question is, is it fair for us to pay $1.5 billion to SHPL?

sections.label: Termination sum fairness formula
sections.summary: The passage states the fairness question concerns a termination sum based on a formula in the PPP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Then, the question about whether it is fair.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This is a termination sum that is based on a formula in the PPP.

sections.label: SHPL annual payment purposes
sections.summary: The $193.7 million paid yearly to SHPL covers loan servicing, interest, operations, maintenance and lifecycle sinking fund costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: One, to service the loan that we would have taken, or at least to account for the interest of that loan; and second, a commitment to an income stream that would allow the project to run, operate, maintain, keep a sinking fund for lifecycle costs and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And when we pay every year, the $193.7 million towards SHPL, that is what those sums are for.

sections.label: Thorough review before decision
sections.summary: A thorough review before the decision examined performance, SportSG internal capabilities, resources, international marquee commitment and possible partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In terms of doing a review, what had been done leading up to this decision was a very thorough review already.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And that review went into aspects, such as where they performed well, where they did not perform so well, looking at the internal capabilities within SportSG, whether we could muscle up enough resources to do what they are doing, the extent to which we feel we can commit to doing this on an international marquee basis, the kind of partners that we might have in Singapore.

sections.label: Payment to private consortium
sections.summary: The Minister says the $193.7 million yearly payment to the private consortium is what the contract says, not generosity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Can I ask the Minister why the Government is so generous to pay $193.7 million a year to the private consortium when he just mentioned also that the operating cost, after we take over, will be about $68 million?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: One, it is not about being generous, this is what the contract says.

sections.label: Debt servicing share of payment
sections.summary: The debt servicing amount is about 65% of the $193.7 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The debt servicing amount, to my memory, is about 65% of the $193.7 million.

sections.label: Deductions for non-performance
sections.summary: A provision for deductions for non-performance or non-availability was confirmed, and the precise amount charged from 2014 will be checked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The then-Minister for MCCY confirmed that there was a provision for deductions in the event of non-performance or non-availability for use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can I just confirm that from 2014 to date, how much has the Government, by way of liquidated damages or whatever the clause in the PPP contract states, charged SHPL for non-performance?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But as I have said, I will check the precise figure since he is asking for something from 2014 until, I take it, this point in time.
